## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Root cause:** Gateway connection pool exhaustion, triggered by deploy `dep-4471` (a.novak, gateway, finished 2026-03-14T02:14:00Z) — "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation." The pool got pinned at `in_use=20` immediately after, with `waiting` climbing steadily and never draining. First WARN at 02:14:14.920Z, first hard 503 at 02:14:18.972Z, 19 seconds after the deploy finished.

**Impact window:** 2026-03-14T02:14:18Z through at least 03:59:27Z (end of captured log — incident was still ongoing, unresolved, no recovery event recorded). Roughly 1h45m+ of intermittent 503s on gateway endpoints (`/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/orders`), recurring in bursts approximately every 4 minutes, with latency and queue depth (`waiting`) both trending up over the window (13 → 74+ waiters, 659ms → 850ms+ request time on failures).

**Scope:** Gateway only. Checked `worker.log` for the same window — no ERRORs, no 503s, `db_wait` stayed low throughout. Workers have a separate DB pool and were unaffected. One unrelated pre-existing WARN in worker.log at 02:36:22Z (slow query, known issue OPS-2210) — not connected to this incident.

**Recommended action:** Roll back `dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak, "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"). Other deploys in the window (`dep-4472` billing 02:41Z, `dep-4473` catalog 03:20Z) landed after the incident already started and are not implicated.
